Merit-based awards require a minimum overall GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, and applicants must show significant leadership or service. Non-merit donor scholarships may accept a minimum 2.5 GPA at the individual donor’s discretion. Applicants seeking funding for a second degree at a level they already hold are ineligible.</li><li><strong>Awards:</strong> Varies</li><li><strong>Total Amount:</strong> $500–$5,000 for merit-based scholarships; $500–$1,000 for non-merit-based donor scholarships</li><li><strong>Application:</strong> The 2026 deadline was 11:59 p.m. PST on May 8, 2026, and recipients are notified by email in August; the sponsor’s page does not yet list the next deadline. The application includes a personal statement, a resume, a peer letter and a faculty letter of recommendation, an official transcript, a photo and a biographical sketch.</li></ul><h2 class="">HIMSS Foundation Scholarship</h2><p class="">The Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society (HIMSS) Foundation awards scholarships to students in degree programs related to health information technology and healthcare management systems.</p><ul><li><strong>Qualifications:</strong> Applicants must be current HIMSS Student Members in good standing and enrolled in an accredited program related to health information technology or healthcare management systems. Undergraduate applicants must be at least first-term juniors. HIMSS employees, consultants, board or advisory board members, scholarship judges and previous HIMSS Foundation Scholarship recipients are not eligible.</li><li><strong>Awards:</strong> One undergraduate scholarship and one graduate scholarship</li><li><strong>Total Amount:</strong> $5,000 each</li><li><strong>Application:</strong> The application requires a resume or CV and one letter of recommendation. The sponsor’s page lists the application as closed and still says the 2027 application would open in August 2026, so check the page for the current status. Many local HIMSS chapters also offer scholarships to student members.</li></ul><h2 class="">AFCEA Shrader Graduate Scholarship</h2><p class="">The AFCEA Educational Foundation awards the Shrader Graduate Scholarship to full-time graduate students in STEM fields that support the defense, homeland security and intelligence communities. Booz Allen Hamilton is the signature sponsor, and the funds can be used only for tuition and course-related expenses.</p><ul><li><strong>Qualifications:</strong> Applicants must be U.S. citizens living in the United States, enrolled in at least their second semester of a graduate program at an accredited U.S. institution, taking two or more semester-equivalent courses, carrying a minimum overall GPA of 3.5 and able to demonstrate financial need. The expected graduation date cannot fall in the calendar year the scholarship is awarded. The major must be on AFCEA’s list of qualifying majors, which includes computer science, information science, mathematics, operations research and statistics. Data science is not named on the list, so applicants in data science programs should confirm that their program fits a listed major.</li><li><strong>Awards:</strong> Not stated by the sponsor</li><li><strong>Total Amount:</strong> $3,000</li><li><strong>Application:</strong> Applications open January 1, 2027. They include an application form, a current official graduate transcript, an undergraduate transcript (official or unofficial), two faculty letters of recommendation in the major field and a current résumé; the sponsor lists May 1, 2027 as the latest date for mailed official documents.</li></ul><h2 class="">MinneAnalytics Data Science Scholarship</h2><p class="">Faculty or staff at institutions can submit applications for their school to award a MinneAnalytics Data Science Scholarship, which targets undergraduate students. Each department or school can receive one scholarship a year, and MinneAnalytics can send the funds to the student, the department or the school’s foundation.</p><ul><li><strong>Qualifications:</strong> Candidates must be current undergraduate students pursuing a STEM education applicable to data science or analytics, display a passion for pursuing a career directly related to data science or analytics and have an ongoing commitment to community engagement.</li><li><strong>Awards:</strong> The sponsor’s past announcements profile 33 <a href="https://minneanalytics.org/meet-the-2021-minneanalytics-scholarship-recipients/" rel="noreferrer noopener" target="_blank" class="underline transition-colors external-link">recipients for 2021–22</a> and 15 <a href="https://minneanalytics.org/meet-the-2025-minneanalytics-scholarship-recipients/" rel="noreferrer noopener" target="_blank" class="underline transition-colors external-link">recipients for 2024–25</a>; these are historical profiles, not current award counts</li><li><strong>Total Amount:</strong> The sponsor’s current page does not state a per-award amount</li><li><strong>Application:</strong> Students cannot apply directly, because a faculty or staff member submits the application. The sponsor’s page lists the 2025–2026 application period as closed and directs readers to its email newsletter for updates.</li></ul><h2 class="">Seth Bonder Scholarship for Applied Operations Research in Health Services</h2><p class="">The Seth Bonder Scholarship for Applied Operations Research in Health Services, offered in conjunction with the Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS), aims to promote the development and application of process modeling and operations research analyses to the design, delivery and operations of health care.</p><ul><li><strong>Qualifications:</strong> This scholarship is for doctoral students, not master’s students. Applicants must have completed at least one but no more than three academic years in a doctoral program and be working at the intersection of operations research or operations management and health care. The <a href="https://connect.informs.org/healthapplications/awards/bonder-scholarship" rel="noreferrer noopener" target="_blank" class="underline transition-colors external-link">application requirements</a> include a CV, two letters of support (one from the main advisor), a one-page career goals statement and a three-page research summary.</li><li><strong>Awards:</strong> One</li><li><strong>Total Amount:</strong> $4,000, plus up to $1,000 for travel to the annual INFORMS conference and an additional $2,000 provided and funded by the Seth Bonder Foundation</li><li><strong>Application:</strong> The 2026 application was due June 30, 2026, with results announced by September 15, 2026. The sponsor’s page does not yet list dates for the next cycle.</li></ul><h2 class="">SMART Scholarship Program</h2><p class="">The Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation (SMART) Scholarship-for-Service Program, funded by the U.S. Department of War (DoW), gives bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral students in approved STEM disciplines full tuition, an annual stipend, summer internships and a civilian job with the DoW after graduation.</p><ul><li><strong>Qualifications:</strong> Applicants must be citizens of the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand or the United Kingdom, be at least 18 years old by January 1, 2028, maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, plan to attend or be enrolled at a regionally accredited U.S. college or university and be able to obtain a security clearance. They must request between one and five years of degree funding, complete summer internships for awards longer than 1.5 years and accept a one-for-one service commitment as a DoW civilian employee. Data Science and Analytics is one of the approved <a href="https://www.smartscholarship.org/smart/en?id=smart_eligibility" rel="noreferrer noopener" target="_blank" class="underline transition-colors external-link">eligibility disciplines</a>, and non-technical degrees are not funded.</li><li><strong>Awards:</strong> The sponsor reports 6,510 scholarships awarded to date</li><li><strong>Total Amount:</strong> Full tuition plus an <a href="https://dowstem.us/participate/smart/" rel="noreferrer noopener" target="_blank" class="underline transition-colors external-link">annual stipend</a> of $30,000–$46,000 depending on degree level, with health and book allowances</li><li><strong>Application:</strong> Applications open each year from August 1 to the first Friday in December.</li></ul><h2 class="">UPE/ACM Scholarship</h2><p class=""><a href="https://upe.acm.org/" rel="noreferrer noopener" target="_blank" class="underline transition-colors external-link">Upsilon Pi Epsilon</a> (UPE), an international honor society for the computing and information disciplines, and the ACM offer the UPE/ACM Scholarship to ACM student members who are about to enter the computing profession.</p><ul><li><strong>Qualifications:</strong> Candidates must be full-time undergraduate or graduate students who are ACM members and also members of the ACM student chapter at their institution. Judges weigh academic records, the faculty member’s recommendation and chapter or department activities.</li><li><strong>Awards:</strong> Four</li><li><strong>Total Amount:</strong> $1,500 each</li><li><strong>Application:</strong> The 2026 deadline was September 30, 2026, and the sponsor’s page does not yet list the next one. Applications go to the sponsor by email as PDF files with official transcripts. UPE members can also apply for the separate UPE Scholarship Awards of $1,000 to $4,000, which are due October 31, 2026.</li></ul><h2 class="">Wellington HBCU Scholars Program</h2><p class="">The Wellington HBCU Scholars Program consists of a renewable, merit-based scholarship of up to $15,000 a year granted to students at historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs) and includes a paid summer internship after the scholar’s sophomore and junior years.</p><ul><li><strong>Qualifications:</strong> The sponsor’s careers page describes the program as serving students at HBCUs but does not publish eligibility terms such as GPA, eligible majors or residency. The sponsor’s dedicated program page could not be opened on October 29, 2026, so confirm eligibility with Wellington before applying.</li><li><strong>Awards:</strong> Not stated on the sponsor’s careers page</li><li><strong>Total Amount:</strong> Up to $15,000, renewable annually and applied to junior- and senior-year tuition</li><li><strong>Application:</strong> Current application instructions were not available when this page was checked on October 29, 2026, because the sponsor’s program page could not be opened. Confirm the application steps and deadline with Wellington.</li></ul><h2 class="">FAQs About Data Science Scholarships</h2><p class="">Students seeking data science scholarships should follow the application instructions carefully and submit materials that verify their eligibility. Here are more FAQs to consider:</p><h3 class="">Are there any scholarships for master’s in data science?</h3><p class="">Yes. Eight of the 11 scholarships above accept master’s students: the ACM SIGHPC fellowship, the Native Forward (AIGC) science scholarship, ASA Pride, Great Minds in STEM, the HIMSS Foundation Scholarship, the AFCEA Shrader Graduate Scholarship, SMART and UPE/ACM. Some name data science or statistics directly, while others cover STEM broadly or a related field such as health information technology. MinneAnalytics and Wellington are for undergraduates, and the Seth Bonder Scholarship is for doctoral students. For more options, students can check the list of data science scholarships above.</p><h3 class="">What are the qualifications to receive a data science scholarship?</h3><p class="">Some scholarships are based on age, ethnicity, minimum GPA, education level, or post-graduate employment requirements. Other factors may be included in the criteria, depending on the sponsoring organization. Among the scholarships above, minimum GPAs range from 2.5 to 3.5. The 2.5 figure applies only to some non-merit Great Minds in STEM donor awards, at the donor’s discretion. SMART and the AFCEA Shrader Graduate Scholarship set citizenship requirements, HIMSS and UPE/ACM require membership, and SIGHPC and MinneAnalytics require a nomination or submission from an advisor or school. SMART also requires post-graduation service.</p><h3 class="">When should I start preparing for a data science scholarship?</h3><p class="">Application deadlines vary throughout the year, and preparation should begin as early as possible because the process may depend on the materials applicants need to collect. They may be required to request and submit transcripts and letters of recommendation, write essays, and fill out forms. Sponsors’ windows differ: SMART accepts applications from August 1 to the first Friday in December, ASA Pride nominations are due March 1, SIGHPC nominations close April 30, 2027 and the AFCEA Shrader Graduate Scholarship opens January 1, 2027. Because several programs need a letter from a faculty member or advisor, ask recommenders well before the deadline. Our <a href="/resources/guide-stem-scholarships/" class="underline transition-colors">guide to STEM scholarships</a> covers organizing applications and writing a personal statement.</p><h3 class="">Can international students apply for data science scholarships?</h3><p class="">Some programs accept them. The SIGHPC fellowship funds study at institutions anywhere in the world, and SMART is open to citizens of the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the United Kingdom, with a service commitment as a Department of War civilian employee. The AFCEA Shrader Graduate Scholarship requires U.S. citizenship, and the Native Forward (AIGC) fund is for American Indian and Alaska Native students who attend accredited U.S. institutions and document their Tribal affiliation. Great Minds in STEM requires enrollment at a college in the U.S. or its territories, and several other sponsors do not state a citizenship rule on their pages, so confirm with the sponsor before applying.</p><h3 class="">Do any data science scholarships require work after graduation?</h3><p class="">SMART does. Recipients commit to one year of Department of War civilian employment at their sponsoring facility for every year of SMART-funded study. The sponsors’ pages for the other scholarships above do not list a service requirement.</p><h3 class="">Can I apply for a scholarship before I enroll in a master’s program?</h3><p class="">It depends on the sponsor. SIGHPC accepts nominations for students who have been accepted to begin a graduate program by October 15 of the nomination year, and SMART accepts applicants who plan to attend a regionally accredited U.S. institution. Great Minds in STEM requires enrollment for the upcoming fall semester, while the AFCEA Shrader Graduate Scholarship requires at least one completed semester of graduate study and ASA Pride requires current enrollment or a recent degree. Applicants who are still applying to programs may find our <a href="/data-science/masters/statement-of-purpose/" class="underline transition-colors">statement of purpose guide</a> useful.</p><h3 class="">Where else can I find funding for a master’s in data science?</h3><p class="">Scholarships are one part of paying for graduate study. <a href="https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types" rel="noreferrer noopener" target="_blank" class="underline transition-colors external-link">Federal Student Aid</a> describes four main types of financial aid: grants, work-study jobs, scholarships and loans. A grant generally does not have to be repaid, a loan must be repaid with interest, and many nonprofit and private organizations offer scholarships. Many schools also offer aid from their own grant and scholarship funds. Our guide on <a href="/learning/research-financial-aid/" class="underline transition-colors">how to research financial aid</a> for STEM programs explains each type.</p><!--]--><!----></div></div><p
